column1: Spillover Effects of US Monetary Policy on Emerging Markets Amidst Uncertainty

The thesis titled Spillover Effects of US Monetary Policy on Emerging Markets Amidst Uncertainty by Povilas Lastauskas and Anh Dinh Minh Nguyen explores the impact of US monetary policy tightening on emerging markets  focusing on both direct and indirect spillover effects. Utilizing a global vector autoregression model with stochastic volatility across 32 countries  the study finds that an increase in US interest rates significantly reduces output in emerging markets  leading to more prolonged and persistent declines. This effect is exacerbated by global trade integration  which causes a sharper but slightly quicker rebounding output drop. The spillover effects are notably amplified when US monetary policy tightening coincides with increased monetary policy uncertainty. The research highlights the considerable heterogeneity in how emerging markets respond to US monetary policy shocks.

The paper begins by contextualizing the issue within the broader economic landscape  noting the significant influence of US monetary policy on global financial cycles. It emphasizes the complexity added by a rising US dollar  which challenges emerging markets' central banks in maintaining local currency stability. The study underscores the importance of understanding both direct and indirect impacts of US monetary policy  as even countries with weak direct links to the US can be affected through their trade or financial connections with other impacted economies.

The authors contribute to the literature by developing a comprehensive global empirical macroeconomic model that covers nearly 90% of the world output. This model allows for the quantification of the direct and indirect impacts of US monetary policy changes on emerging markets. The study also distinguishes between the effects of monetary policy shocks and those of monetary policy uncertainty  particularly in the context of the high inflation environment of 2022-2023. The research is pioneering in quantifying spillover strengths while accounting for changes in policy and macroeconomic uncertainty.

The findings reveal that US monetary policy tightening reduces output growth and inflation  but also increases US macroeconomic volatility  especially inflation volatility. The study highlights the role of financial markets as a crucial channel for US monetary policy spillovers  with the magnitude and dynamics of international reactions depending on the nature of the US economic shock. The research provides new insights into the global financial cycle driven by US monetary policy  emphasizing the need for emerging markets to consider both direct and indirect effects when formulating their economic strategies.
